component.name: Apache Ignite
component.description: Distributed database and computing platform (Ignite 3). Security comprises two independent layers: an authentication layer validating client identity through configured providers, and a transport encryption layer protecting communication channels (node-to-node, client-to-node, and REST API) with SSL/TLS. The security model assumes network perimeter protection as a prerequisite.

externalReferences.comment: Source security model document; this file is a structured translation of it.

blueprints.name: Ignite 3 cluster deployment
blueprints.description: Architecture described by the Ignite 3 security documentation: cluster nodes communicate over node-to-node channels inside a protected subnetwork; external clients connect over client-to-node channels and the REST API; an authentication manager coordinates sequential provider attempts, and three independent SSL configurations govern the distinct communication channels.

assets.name: Cluster node
assets.description: Server node of the Ignite 3 cluster. By having access to any cluster node it is possible to perform malicious actions on the cluster; all server node network ports must operate exclusively within protected subnetworks.

assets.name: Authentication manager
assets.description: Coordinates sequential authentication provider attempts; the first successful validation grants access. Built-in basic username/password authentication is configured via cluster settings; custom providers (server-side Authenticator, configuration schema extension, client-side IgniteClientAuthenticator) enable external identity provider, LDAP, or custom credential store integration.

assets.name: REST API
assets.description: REST endpoints with a separate, independent SSL configuration.

zones.name: Protected cluster subnetwork
zones.description: Protected subnetwork (DMZ) in which all server node network ports must operate exclusively.

zones.name: External clients
zones.description: Clients connecting over client-to-node connections and the REST API, authenticated by the configured providers.

assumptions.description: The security posture assumes network perimeter protection as a prerequisite: all server node network ports operate exclusively within protected subnetworks, and external exposure requires SSL certificate controls from trusted Certification Authorities.
The authentication and transport encryption layers function independently, but production environments should activate both.

threats.name: Malicious actions from a compromised cluster node
threats.description: By having access to any cluster node it is possible to perform malicious actions on the cluster. There are no protective mechanisms against threats originating from compromised nodes; the model relies on keeping server node ports within protected subnetworks.

threats.name: Credential interception with basic authentication over unencrypted transport
threats.description: Basic authentication transmits credentials unencrypted when SSL/TLS is not enabled; production deployments mandate encryption enablement.

threats.name: Access by clients without validated identity
threats.description: Client identity is validated by the configured authentication providers; the authentication manager attempts providers sequentially and the first successful validation grants access. Without authentication enabled, client access is not identity-checked.

threats.name: Interception or tampering of unencrypted communication channels
threats.description: Node-to-node cluster communication, client-to-node connections, and REST API endpoints are protected by SSL/TLS only when the corresponding SSL configuration is enabled; each of the three channels is governed by an independent configuration.

threats.name: Equivalent resource access for all authenticated users (no authorization)
threats.description: Apache Ignite 3 currently provides authentication only. Authorization features (role-based access control, permissions) are not yet implemented; all authenticated users possess equivalent cluster resource access.

trustBoundaries.name: Client access boundary
trustBoundaries.description: Clients connect using authenticator objects corresponding to configured providers; without SSL/TLS, basic authentication credentials cross this boundary in cleartext.

trustBoundaries.name: REST API boundary
trustBoundaries.description: Separate SSL configuration secures REST endpoint access independently.

controls.name: Operate server ports only within protected subnetworks
controls.description: All server node network ports must operate exclusively within protected subnetworks (DMZ); external exposure requires SSL certificate controls from trusted Certification Authorities.

controls.name: Enable authentication providers
controls.description: Configure the built-in basic username/password authentication via cluster settings, or a custom provider (server-side Authenticator, configuration schema extension, and client-side IgniteClientAuthenticator) to integrate an external identity provider, LDAP, or a custom credential store.

controls.name: Enable SSL/TLS on all communication channels
controls.description: Three independent SSL configurations govern node-to-node cluster communication, client-to-node connections, and REST API endpoints; configuration involves keystore/truststore paths, passwords, cipher specifications, and client authentication requirements (none/optional/required). Production deployments must enable encryption, since basic authentication otherwise transmits credentials unencrypted.

controls.name: Mutual TLS between cluster members
controls.description: Node-to-node SSL deployment with clientAuth=require establishes mutual TLS verification between cluster members.

controls.name: Audit authentication events
controls.description: Authentication attempts generate auditable events: USER_AUTHENTICATION_SUCCESS and USER_AUTHENTICATION_FAILURE.
